content: To sustain a representation, to hold it steady before the mind against distracting ideas, is the sovereign victory of the moral will.
author: William James
sourceWork: Pragmatism: A New Name for Some Old Ways of Thinking (1907)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

In William James's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
